assertion_analysis.failure_condition: Removing the shadow block from _review_brief_text makes the git -C diff command, the ls-files command and the contract sentence all absent, so the assertion fails; confirmed by negative-control-remove-block.log.
A block that hardcoded a fixed worktree or base, or read them from the wrong record, would leave the second record's tree absent or the first tree present; the assertion fails.
Appending any block for a non-shadow changes the composed text from load_review_prompt() plus the identity lines and injects the contract sentence; the assertion fails.
Appending the block for every paired arm rather than for a shadow injects "shadow" into the paired primary's brief; the assertion fails, confirmed by negative-control-paired-arm.log.

findings.text: follow-on: the first case asserts the block echoes the worktree and base the test itself supplied, and HEAD is set equal to BASE_SHA (lines 28-29), so the assertion cannot tell a block reading base_sha from one reading head; the second case (lines 96-99) supplies the independent check that the block reads from the record, which limits the gap to the base-versus-head indistinguishability.
